source_text: nudum operuerit, periclitantem liberaverit, aegri vulnera foverit, divitias honestae amicitiae impenderit, ad testimonium falsum nec tormentis potuerit impelli
pass_a_gloss: Nudum operuerit, periclitantem liberaverit, aegri vulnera foverit, divitias honestae amicitiae impenderit, to testimony false nor tormentis potuerit impelli.
pass_b_english: If a pagan clothes a naked person, is it a sin because it is not from faith?
If a pagan clothes a naked person, rescues someone in danger, tends a sick person’s wounds, spends their wealth in honorable friendship, and cannot be forced even by torture to give false testimony…

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
